title: Voicevelo G-major, enough to win gravel races??

takeaways.text: The frameset costs US$2,999, which he calls not cheap for a Chinese frame; the bar and stem are bought separately, and the package includes a bottom bracket and computer mount.
The inside of the carbon looked well finished, and he rates the build quality highly, as with his earlier Voicevelo road frame.
It clears 47 mm tires front and rear, which he finds enough although many new gravel frames offer 55 mm; his 45 mm Hutchinson tires measure 47 mm, exactly the maximum.
The frame has a T47 bottom bracket, UDH and many bag mounts, and a claimed weight of 790 g; size L is 54 and XL (57) is the largest, so it does not suit very tall riders.
After a few tarmac rides only, it feels fast with good bottom-bracket stiffness; gravel comfort and race handling were still to be tested.

disclosure: Former pro rider's build and first-ride video; how he obtained the frame is not stated.
summary: Ide Schelling builds a size-L Voicevelo G Major with Voicevelo Kevlar-spoked wheels and gives first road impressions.
